source: pdfsource/_pages_thyroidv8/ (Thyroid Differentiated and Anaplastic Carcinoma Quick Reference; anaplastic stage table on p5)

categories.description: Primary tumor cannot be assessed
No evidence of primary tumor
Tumor less than or equal to 2 cm in greatest dimension limited to the thyroid (parent for T1a/T1b)
Tumor less than or equal to 1 cm in greatest dimension limited to the thyroid
Tumor greater than 1 cm but less than or equal to 2 cm in greatest dimension limited to the thyroid
Tumor greater than 2 cm but less than or equal to 4 cm in greatest dimension limited to the thyroid
Tumor greater than 4 cm limited to the thyroid, or gross extrathyroidal extension invading only strap muscles (parent for T3a/T3b)
Tumor greater than 4 cm limited to the thyroid
Gross extrathyroidal extension invading only strap muscles (sternohyoid, sternothyroid, thyrohyoid, or omohyoid muscles) from a tumor of any size
Includes gross extrathyroidal extension, beyond the strap muscles (parent for T4a/T4b)
Gross extrathyroidal extension invading subcutaneous soft tissues, larynx, trachea, esophagus, or recurrent laryngeal nerve from a tumor of any size
Gross extrathyroidal extension invading prevertebral fascia or encasing the carotid artery or mediastinal vessels from a tumor of any size

notes.definitions: These definitions apply to Papillary, Follicular, Poorly Differentiated, Hurthle Cell, and Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma. All categories may be subdivided: (s) solitary tumor and (m) multifocal tumor. The largest tumor determines the classification.

categories.description: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
No evidence of locoregional lymph node metastasis (parent for N0a/N0b)
One or more cytologically or histologically confirmed benign lymph nodes
No radiologic or clinical evidence of locoregional lymph node metastasis
Metastasis to regional nodes (parent for N1a/N1b)
Metastasis to level VI or VII (pretracheal, paratracheal, or prelaryngeal/Delphian, or upper mediastinal) lymph nodes. This can be unilateral or bilateral disease.
Metastasis to unilateral, bilateral, or contralateral lateral neck lymph nodes (levels I, II, III, IV, or V) or retropharyngeal lymph nodes
No distant metastasis
Distant metastasis
Clinical classification.
Pathological classification.

categories.description: Post-neoadjuvant.
No neoadjuvant therapy.

notes.matching: DescY does not affect the anaplastic stage outcome.

categories.description: Recurrent.
Not recurrent.

notes.matching: DescR is recorded for context and ignored by the rule lookup.

categories.description: Multiple synchronous primaries.
Single primary tumor.
